newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-HERBERT FOCUSED ON MEDAL-WINNING DISPLAY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HERBERT FOCUSED ON MEDAL-WINNING DISPLAY.

text.p: Top South African hurdler Llewellyn Herbert, armed with a modified stride pattern and a sequence of impressive times this year, is focused on a medal- winning performance at the Athens world championships in August.

The 19-year-old, who broke the South African record for the 400-metre hurdles with an explosive 48.35 seconds in Pietersburg in February, is confident he can dip under the 48-second mark against quality competition in Greece.
"In Athens, I want to run a sub-48 because I want to win there -- that final will be the whole focus of my year," Herbert told Reuters.
"My best so far is 48.35 and I'm confident of going under that in Athens if things go well. With good competition and tough guys against me, I really believe I can do a sub-48 seconds."
Herbert's most recent run was an impressive 49.27 seconds in the Southern Region track and field athletics championships at Durban's Kings Park soccer stadium on Sunday.
Well out of the regular southern hemisphere athletics season, this time was more or less what Herbert had predicted, and it was even more impressive in that it was posted at sea level.
"Before the race, I said I wanted to run a low 49 seconds in Durban, and I did. I then knew that my preparation for Athens was well on course," Herbert said afterwards.
Herbert believes his modified stride pattern which he introduced before the world juniors in Australia last year has been the significant factor in his faster times so far this year.
"My stride pattern was left leg all the way and I've since changed it to left-right, left-right. I used that pattern in Durban at the weekend and it's going pretty well at the moment.
"Earlier on in the year, I struggled a bit but I'm confident it will be ready for Athens. The change was all about faster times and my rhythm is wonderful now. I can't complain about that at all."
The only problem facing Herbert between now and Athens is a distinct lack of quality competition.
He is set to run in a Grand Prix II meeting in Lille, France this Sunday but otherwise his manager Peet van Zyl has struggled to get him into any other races.
"If I don't get any more meetings, Athletics South Africa is organising some races for the athletes in Europe so I hopefully I might compete in some of those," Herbert said.

Van Zyl is hoping to get Herbert into a Grand Prix I meeting in Nice on July 16. Thereafter, Herbert will leave with the South African team for their pre-Athens training camp in Tata, Hungary on July 31.
